title: Due Date of the Initial Service Documentation
content:
**Correspondence unit clause — Hardship and Protective Holds.** On a Military Service Hold request, the initial documentation is due the tier's documentation days after the request date: the days allowed for the initial service documentation run from the day the request letter is sent to that date. The days allowed for the initial service documentation are a whole number of calendar days and are not rounded.

## Quantities

| Quantity | Source |
|---|---|
| Request date | The date the hold request was received, on the hold record |
| The tier's documentation days | The Military Service Hold's documentation due days in the product's documentation standards |
| Due date | The request date plus the tier's documentation days |
| Days allowed | Calendar days from the day the request letter is sent to the due date |

## Worked example (hypothetical)

A Military Service Hold request was received on 2 June. Taking, for the illustration, documentation days of 30, the documentation is due on 2 July. The request letter is sent on 4 June; from 4 June to 2 July is 28 calendar days, so the days allowed are 28.

Had the letter gone out on 2 June itself, the days allowed would be 30.
